title: Bomb Threat & Suspicious Packages
blurb: What to do if you take a bomb threat call or find a suspicious item: stay calm, record, do not touch.
siteNotes: Who the Duty Manager is on each shift and how to reach them quickly
Where a pen and paper or a threat call checklist is kept near the main phones
How the Duty Manager will signal an evacuation
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-33 (the venue's 10-minute trainer). Taught as written.

CHECK: Martyn's Law (the Terrorism (Protection of Premises) Act 2025) places new duties on venues, depending on capacity, with a phased start. Please confirm whether and when it applies to the venue and whether this trainer needs updating.

CHECK: police advice on suspicious items is often summarised as HOT (Hidden, Obviously suspicious, Typical). The trainer's "do not touch" and alert-the-Duty-Manager approach is taught as written; confirm it matches current counter-terrorism guidance.

cards.title: Bomb Threat & Suspicious Packages
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- stay calm and take a threat call properly
- recognise a suspicious item and not touch it
- know who makes the decisions

cards.title: Rare, but we treat every one seriously
cards.body: Thankfully this is rare. The overwhelming majority of threats turn out to be hoaxes, but we treat every one seriously. Staying calm and following a simple procedure is what keeps everyone safe.

items.title: Mostly hoaxes
items.text: Most threats turn out to be hoaxes.

items.title: Calm helps
items.text: A simple procedure keeps people safe.

cards.title: Keep them talking
cards.body: If you take a threat over the phone, keep the caller talking for as long as you can and gather information. Do not hang up first. As soon as the call ends, alert the Duty Manager immediately.

left.title: Do
items: Note their exact words and the time
Note the number if it shows
Alert the Duty Manager at once

cards.title: What to note about the call
cards.body: Write down what you can. Even small details help.

cards.title: Do not touch
cards.body: If you find an unattended bag, a package that does not belong, or something that just feels wrong, remember the phrase: do not touch.

items.title: Do not touch
items.text: Do not move, open, cover or investigate it.

items.title: Keep people away
items.text: Keep people well away from it.

items.title: Follow instructions
items.text: The Duty Manager decides what happens next.

cards.title: The Duty Manager leads
cards.body: The Duty Manager leads the response and makes the call on evacuating and contacting the police, including 999. Your job is to stay calm, record what you can, avoid touching anything suspicious, and follow instructions. Panic helps no one.

items.title: You
items.text: Stay calm, record, do not touch, follow instructions.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Treat every threat seriously, even though most are hoaxes
- On a threat call, keep the caller talking and note everything
- Alert the Duty Manager immediately
- Suspicious item: do not touch, keep people away
- The Duty Manager decides on evacuation and 999

cards.q: Most bomb threats turn out to be hoaxes, but we treat every one seriously.
cards.why: The overwhelming majority are hoaxes, but staying calm and following the procedure every time is what keeps everyone safe.

cards.q: On a threat call you should…
options: Hang up immediately and call the police
Shout for everyone to run
Put the caller on hold to find a manager
Keep the caller talking and note details
cards.why: Keep the caller talking for as long as you can and gather information. Do not hang up first.

cards.q: Which of these should you note about a threat call?
options: Their exact words, the time, and any background noise
Whether the caller sounds like a regular guest
Only the time of the call
What you think the caller wants to hear
cards.why: Note exact words, the time, voice, accent, background noise and the number if shown. Every detail may help.

cards.q: You should move a suspicious package to a safer spot.
cards.why: Do not touch it. Do not move, open, cover or investigate it. Keep people away instead.

cards.q: When you find a suspicious item you should…
options: Open it to check what it is
Cover it up so guests do not see it
Not touch it and keep people away
Ask a guest if it belongs to them
cards.why: Remember "do not touch". Keep people well away and alert the Duty Manager.

cards.q: After a threat call, you should alert the Duty Manager immediately.
cards.why: As soon as the call ends, alert the Duty Manager immediately so they can lead the response.

cards.q: Who decides on evacuation and calling 999?
options: You alone
The caller
The first person to hear about it
The Duty Manager
cards.why: The Duty Manager leads the response and makes the call on evacuating and contacting the police.

cards.q: Panicking is the best way to keep people safe.
cards.why: Panic helps no one. A calm, practised response is what keeps guests and colleagues safe.

cards.q: What three-word phrase applies to a suspicious item?
options: Move it away
Do not touch
Cover and wait
Check and report
cards.why: "Do not touch." Do not move, open, cover or investigate it.

cards.q: If your phone displays the caller's number, you should note it.
cards.why: If the phone shows the number, note it. Together with their words, voice and background noise it helps the response.
